key_insight: A deep learning competing-risk model using only pre-treatment clinical data can identify women with breast cancer at high 1-year cardiovascular risk before therapy starts.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help oncology teams prioritize early cardio-oncology referral and risk-aware treatment planning using information already available at the initial visit.
method: Registry-based cohort of 17,051 women with stage I-III breast cancer or DCIS
Used demographics, cancer features, planned treatment, comorbidities, medications, and healthcare use available before treatment
Trained and validated a deep learning model for 1-year MACE with non-cardiovascular death as a competing risk
evidence_signal: Across 3-fold cross-validation, the model showed strong discrimination with a median c-index of 0.84 for 1-year MACE and 0.90 for the competing-risk outcome.
watch_item: The model was developed in one regional cohort, so external validation is needed before broad clinical deployment.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Based Pretreatment Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Women with Breast Cancer
